summary.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.3% YoY to INR 630.5 crore, with EBITDA margin held at 13.1% despite steeper input inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR 630.5 crore, up 14.3% YoY and 14.9% QoQ, with EBITDA up 19.1% to INR 82.5 crore. EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps YoY to 13.1% and was flat QoQ, while gross margin fell from about 47.2% in Q1 to about 46% on RM and packaging inflation. Domestic biscuits grew low teens, bakery (English Oven, NaturBaked, Cremica bakery) grew high teens, and exports grew more slowly on Middle East disruption and freight. Management expects margins to stay under pressure in Q3 and to recover toward 13.5-14% in Q4.

segments.name: Domestic biscuits
segments.commentary: Grew low teens in Q2 (excluding agencies); volume growth was about 4-5%, with the balance from price. Management targets high single-digit then double-digit volume growth over coming quarters.

segments.name: Exports (biscuits)
segments.commentary: Growth slowed in Q2 due to Middle East disruption, freight spikes and delayed container pickups. Management still guides to mid-teens export growth for FY27.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, NaturBaked, frozen)
segments.commentary: Grew high teens in value and mid-teens in volume in Q2; bakery is about twice the size of institutional bakery. Quick commerce and general trade distribution expansion are the main drivers; NaturBaked runs at about INR 1-1.5 crore per month.

segments.name: Institutional bakery
segments.commentary: Grew mid-to-high teens in both volume and value in Q2, with QSR recovery cited. Ongoing B2B store expansion by partners.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens; H2 growth forecast at mid-to-high teens, supported by price increases taken late Q2 and partly in Q3.
Price increase of about 3% taken in Q2 over Q1; full-year FY27 price increase now expected around 5-6%. Further increases in October, partly carrying into November.
Q3 EBITDA margin targeted to hold near 13.1%; Q4 targeted at 13.5-14%. Gross margin expected to hold at current levels through Q3 and Q4.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 14-15% reaffirmed; 14% is the first milestone.
Bakery growth of 20%+ is achievable in the medium term, with a mix of outsourcing and in-house capacity (Punjab a likely capacity location).
Biscuit distribution target by 2030 of 900,000 to 1 million outlets; current reach about 7 lakh outlets per AC Nielsen for biscuits.
capex_capacity: Added over 30,000 of the targeted 40,000 INR 245+ billing outlets in the 400-500 km radius of the Rajpura plant in H1; now about 345,000 outlets in the defined geography. Added 10-15% more distributors.
Bakery outlet reach about 45,000-50,000; English Oven added about 12,000-13,000 outlets over the last year (about 20-22% growth).
New Kolkata and Khopoli bakery units are scaling up; Hyderabad opened last year; a partner unit was started in Lucknow.
Bakery capacity: Mumbai adequate for a couple of years; Punjab may need new capacity; outsourcing used for non-core products while core products stay in-house for quality control.
Cremica Preferred Outlets contribute 13-14% of volume; target is 20%.
demand_pricing: Domestic biscuit price parity with the best competitors has been reached; volume growth is about 4-5% and is driven by distribution expansion and throughput per outlet.
Biscuit price hikes are largely delivered via de-grammage in the 5 and 10 rupee packs (about 70% of biscuit contribution); management did not disclose the grammage-cut percentage.
English Oven price increases are passed through as MRP increases, with industry-wide pass-through.
Organised trade is 43-44% of bakery sales in Q2 and rising QoQ; quick commerce now about 22% of combined bakery and biscuit B2C sales.
Quick commerce margins are higher than general trade, due to procurement efficiency, freight and lower replacement costs, while marketing spend is higher in that channel.
Export shipping and freight costs were severely affected by the West Asia conflict; Middle East business was hit, though freight is showing early easing signs.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition in north and central India biscuits, given large players and regional players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intensity is high from large and regional players; the company is responding through distribution expansion, 10-15% more distributors, and quick commerce premium launches (shortbread with 25% butter, Zero Maida coconut biscuit), with three new quick commerce products planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook for revenue and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year revenue growth expected to end at mid-teens. Q3 margin target is to hold around 13.1%, and Q4 is targeted at 13.5-14%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the bread (bakery) growth and how did institutional and retail split?
qa_highlights.answer: English Oven volume grew mid-teens and value very high-teens; institutional bakery grew mid-to-high teens in both volume and value. English Oven CAGR has been high-teens for five years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports slow in Q2, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East exposure, freight spikes and delayed container pickups slowed orders. Relationships are intact and the full-year export outlook is still mid-teens.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase was taken in Q2 and expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 3% in Q2 over Q1; full-year around 5-6%. Further increases in October and partly November.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin dip from Q1 to Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Both raw material and packaging inflation. Price recovery was about 1% short, which accounts for the roughly 1% gap in gross margin. Gross margin is expected to hold at current levels in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14-15% EBITDA margin target still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reaffirmed 14% as the first milestone and 15% after, with Q4 FY27 targeted at 13.5-14%.

risks_watch: Escalation of the West Asia conflict or a sharper turn in food inflation could derail the H2 recovery, per management.
Commodity and packaging inflation peaks in Q3; margins may stay pressured until price increases annualise and Project IMPACT matures.
Export recovery depends on freight easing and delayed Middle East and US shipments being cleared.
Quick commerce competition from new startups in bakery; general trade rivalry with legacy players.
Succession and leadership: no succession plan decided yet; Suvir Bector now oversees domestic biscuits along with exports; Ishaan Bector leads bakery; more to be shared next quarter.
Biscuit volume growth (4-5%) remains well below management's high-single-digit aspiration; grammage cut quantum not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and on delivering margin stability, but cautious on near-term margins, with the company guiding that Q3 faces the steepest commodity pressure. Management was evasive on succession planning and on the grammage-cut quantum, and deferred a number on that to a follow-up.
key_quotes: We are pleased to share that the quarter has delivered on both counts.
we expect margins to remain under pressure in the near term.
Our endeavor would be to protect margins while continuing to invest behind growth.
So as of now, Q-com is better in terms of, higher in terms of margins.

adds.what: Bakery units in Kolkata and Khopoli scaling up; Hyderabad opened last year; partner unit started in Lucknow (no capacity numbers given)
Punjab bakery capacity under consideration, may be needed (no timing or size given)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens (held), H2 at mid-to-high teens backed by a ~3% Q2 price rise and 5-6% full-year pricing, plus 4-5% biscuit volume growth and bakery distribution gains; no hard capacity numbers given for the near term, and the Q4 EBITDA margin target was softened to 13.5-14%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 13.1% in Q2 (+50 bps YoY, flat QoQ) and Q3 is guided to hold near 13.1%, with Q4 at 13.5-14%, but gross margin fell from 47.2% to about 46% on RM and packaging inflation that peaks in Q3.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kolkata and Khopoli bakery units are scaling up and Punjab bakery capacity may be needed, but no capacity sizes or dates were given, and Mumbai is adequate for a couple of years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic biscuit volume grew about 4-5% with 10-15% more distributors added, bakery volume grew mid-teens, and H2 growth is guided at mid-to-high teens, though biscuit volume is well below the high-single-digit aspiration.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Punjab bakery capacity may be needed and bakery growth of 20%+ is targeted with a mix of outsourcing and in-house capacity, but no timing or capex amount was disclosed and utilisation was not given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth was held at mid-teens and the Q4 EBITDA margin target was softened to 13.5-14%, so the call points to no near-term upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged that West Asia escalation or sharper food inflation could derail the H2 recovery, and Q3 faces the steepest commodity pressure, though the mid-teens revenue guide was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three new quick commerce products are planned (shortbread with 25% butter, Zero Maida coconut biscuit), and quick commerce is about 22% of combined bakery and biscuit B2C sales.

rows.label: Further price increases from October
rows.why: Price increase of about 3% taken in Q2 with full-year FY27 pricing now expected at 5-6%, and further increases in October partly carrying into November.

rows.label: Export recovery as freight eases
rows.why: Export growth slowed in Q2 on Middle East disruption and freight, but mid-teens FY27 export growth is still guided and freight shows early easing signs.

rows.label: Outlet distribution expansion to 900k-1m by 2030
rows.why: About 345,000 billing outlets now in the core geography after adding over 30,000 of the 40,000 target in H1, with about 7 lakh biscuit outlets nationally today.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line growth and the 14-15% medium-term margin target but cautious on near-term margins, with Q3 facing the steepest commodity pressure; analysts pushed on competition, the H2 margin path and the grammage cut, which management did not quantify.
